# Verification analysis: redundant-uplinks-centos-stream10

Job: `2026-09-05__03-00-00`

This report explains the verifier decisions recorded for this job. It interprets the saved evidence; it does not rerun the task or independently inspect the expired clusters.

## Task

> `node1` and `node2` are joined by two independent links, and each serves a
> private network holding one host, `node3` and `node4`. Carry traffic between
> the two private networks over both links, and keep `node3` and `node4`
> reaching each other when either one of the links is taken out of service.

- Networks: **mgmt, transit-a, transit-b, lan-a, lan-b**
- Control node: **node3**
- Executor model: **claude-sonnet-5**

## Trial `redundant-uplinks-centos-stream1__GrPzDeA`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** The executor established redundant L3 connectivity between node3's and node4's private networks carried actively over both node1-node2 uplinks (bonded via balance-rr after LACP proved incompatible with the virtio NICs), and directly demonstrated a bounded link-outage-and-recovery cycle showing node3<->node4 connectivity was maintained with 0% loss on the remaining link and full restoration afterward. The mandatory node-restart evidence protocol was completed on all four nodes with matching boot-identity changes independently confirmed by the fixed lifecycle snapshots, and post-restart state (bonding, routes, forwarding, NetworkManager config, cross-subnet ping) was verified recovered. Hygiene is good overall, with one bounded and fully-reverted ARP-monitoring bonding experiment and some leftover diagnostic log files as minor findings.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.750 | 0.870 | 106/1 (+17 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **req-1 — Satisfied:** Carry traffic between node3's and node4's private networks over both independent node1-node2 links (active-active use of both links)
  - **Why:** A Linux bond0 (balance-rr, miimon 100) was created on node1 and node2 spanning eth1+eth2, with 172.20.0.0/30 point-to-point addressing, IP forwarding enabled, and static routes to the opposite 192.168.x.0/24 subnet via bond0. node3->node4 ping succeeded with 0% loss over a 40-packet burst, and tx_packets on both eth1 and eth2 on node1 incremented identically (104->127, +23 each) during that burst, directly demonstrating both physical links carrying traffic (round-robin load balancing). balance-rr was adopted after LACP (802.3ad) failed due to a virtio-net limitation (dmesg showed 'failed to get link speed/duplex'), which is a reasonable, well-documented substitution rather than a shortfall.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-0f843b275ff9425e`, `cmd-325359035dcb4a92`, `cmd-1252471645d7456b`, `cmd-c76cc7515bdd4590`, `cmd-610925e0415c4841`, `cmd-abd4b358ffe34674`, `cmd-f731b1ef61dd4c3c`, `cmd-3ff2648eb04a434c`
- **req-2 — Satisfied:** Keep node3 and node4 reaching each other when either one of the two links is taken out of service
  - **Why:** A healthy baseline (0% loss, cmd-e4a7ab7dcedf406c) was captured, then eth1 was disabled at both node1 and node2 (cmd-909eb0d3d5754798, cmd-c6a273fd271e4464) — the executor documented and demonstrated that the virtual point-to-point links do not propagate one-sided admin-down to the peer (cmd-516ba2c0b861472a, cmd-ed3271c2f17d46db), so a full symmetric link outage was used as the realistic failure model. During the outage, node3->node4 ping showed 0% loss over the remaining link (cmd-aca6c570f9b849c8), and after restoring eth1 (cmd-5eb47c2c6e6b4c7a, cmd-c08de683c1294324) the bond returned to MII up on both slaves and resumed carrying traffic on both links, confirmed by incrementing tx_packets on eth1 and eth2 (cmd-6ba16d7d0ffe445b, cmd-732ea34c97a245f5) and a further 0%-loss ping burst (cmd-cae1127468c241b9). This is a full bounded disruption-and-recovery cycle with direct before/during/after observation.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-e4a7ab7dcedf406c`, `cmd-909eb0d3d5754798`, `cmd-c6a273fd271e4464`, `cmd-3e184f6642cd406f`, `cmd-aca6c570f9b849c8`, `cmd-5eb47c2c6e6b4c7a`, `cmd-c08de683c1294324`, `cmd-124486a0a16c4d4e`, `cmd-6ba16d7d0ffe445b`, `cmd-cae1127468c241b9`, `cmd-732ea34c97a245f5`
- **req-3 — Satisfied:** Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on all four managed nodes with recovered network/service/data state
  - **Why:** For each of node1, node2, node3, node4: a pre-restart boot_id/uptime was captured, a reboot was issued and acknowledged (connection reset/timeout observed during the outage window), a differing post-restart boot_id was captured, and post-restart state (antrieb-links.service active with bonding/routes/forwarding restored on node1/node2; NetworkManager static IP/route intact on node3/node4) plus a successful 0%-loss cross-subnet ping were observed. This matches the fixed after-executor lifecycle snapshot, which independently confirms a changed boot-identity on all four nodes.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-1fe7c86cc22a44f7`, `cmd-c116ca98add84f07`, `cmd-6a02d7168c6a48d9`, `cmd-d86b112ab0734c15`, `cmd-9d790d98a75e4e89`, `cmd-dcc9f9dfac9d458c`, `cmd-5321cf3f28e04275`, `cmd-c84e8e547a6d4f32`, `cmd-edefd7b799444835`, `cmd-9102d6cf93334923`, `cmd-2ec95846afa34ee0`, `cmd-5aa9009c030e4c5d`, `cmd-ab424fa1e3334dab`, `cmd-47089dac300840f4`, `cmd-e98fe19e63fb401b`, `cmd-b1d9ef69ac23401e`, `cmd-05324f61a5de4f47`, `cmd-046fd152f3724493`, `cmd-1273dbc8ccd94c39`, `global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity`, `global:after_executor:node2:boot-identity`, `global:after_executor:node3:boot-identity`, `global:after_executor:node4:boot-identity`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.750**. Most mutations were directly tied to satisfying the material outcomes: bonding config, routing, forwarding, and the persistence unit. One clear unnecessary mutation was identified: an ARP-monitoring bond variant (arp_interval/arp_ip_target/arp_validate) was created on node1 and node2 (cmd-6caa4f05672f45ff, cmd-a2c08f8d60474fce) as a troubleshooting experiment after miimon-based balance-rr was already working; it caused a spurious 'no route to arp_ip_target ... arp_validate is set' condition (visible in dmesg, cmd-82e4d9976e044082) and was fully reverted back to the working miimon-100 configuration (cmd-0594d546415b4d56, cmd-18998bb515784ddf) with no lasting residue — a bounded, low-risk, fully-reverted detour. Additionally, several ephemeral diagnostic files (/tmp/bigping.log, /tmp/p2.log, /tmp/cap_enp8s0.log, /tmp/reboot.log) were left behind on node3/node4 per the after-executor snapshot rather than cleaned up; this is low-severity residue with no functional impact. No failed services, no unsafe exposure, and no damaged package state were introduced (failed-services and package-health observations are identical pre/post aside from pre-existing SONiC health/watchdog failures).

### Comments and limitations

- The failover test disabled the link at both endpoints simultaneously (rather than a true one-sided failure) because the platform's virtual links do not propagate one-sided admin-down to the peer; this is a reasonable adaptation given the documented platform limitation, but it is a slightly different failure model than a single-node link fault.
- Bonding was implemented with balance-rr instead of the originally attempted 802.3ad/LACP due to a virtio-net limitation; this is disclosed by the executor and does not affect the observed outcome, but reviewers should be aware the redundancy mechanism is round-robin bonding rather than LACP.
- Operational hygiene was below a full pass (0.750); review the hygiene explanation above separately from functional success.
- Verifier confidence was 0.870; this is evidence confidence for this trial, not a repeatability estimate.
